question.text: A retirement adviser providing services to prospects outside India can charge an onboarding fee of up to:

answer.text: US$2 when sourcing and sending applications to Indian PoP
US$8 when sourcing applications in the overseas territory
Up to US$8 if sourcing applications in the overseas territory and sending to an Indian PoP, or up to US$2 if submitting to a PoP's overseas branch — depending on the arrangement
There is no fee allowed for overseas prospects

explanation.text: The Logic: If the RA sources applications in overseas territory and sends to Indian PoP: up to US$8. If submitted to the PoP's overseas branch: up to US$2. Subsequent service charges: up to US$1 per transaction. The Trap: The fee depends on where the application is submitted — to an Indian PoP or overseas branch of a PoP. Both US$2 and US$8 are valid caps under different arrangements, so a single-amount choice is incomplete. Cross-Exam Context: Overseas NPS distribution is specific to Series XVII. Few other NISM exams cover cross-border advisory fees. Distributor's Pro-Tip: Understand the fee structure clearly when serving NRI/OCI subscribers. The fee depends on the onboarding arrangement with the PoP.
